title: Communications, Creative and Print Services
description: whg is seeking to appoint suppliers to provide Communications, Creative and Print Services. The procurement is divided into two Lots, with a separate contract to be awarded for each Lot. Suppliers may tender for one or both Lots and may be awarded one or both Lots. Lot 1 - Strategic Creative and Campaign Services whg requires the appointment of a single supplier to act as a strategic communications and creative campaign delivery agency, providing specialist support to the in-house Communications team. The Agency will be expected to deliver insight-led communications and marketing campaigns that achieve measurable outcomes and demonstrate value for money. In addition to campaign delivery, the Agency will act as a strategic partner, providing industry expertise, audience insight, market intelligence and innovative thinking to support whg's longer-term communications objectives. The Agency will be expected to demonstrate a strong understanding of the housing, public and charitable sectors and the ability to engage effectively with a range of stakeholders and key audience groups. Services may include, but are not limited to: • Insight gathering and audience research. • Campaign strategy and planning. • Creative concept development. • Design and creative direction. • Campaign delivery. • Monitoring and reporting. • Post-campaign evaluation. Typical projects may include customer communication campaigns, including service or safety information; recruitment campaigns; organisational change and transformation communications; internal communication and engagement campaigns; and behavioural change campaigns. These examples are illustrative and are not exhaustive. Where campaigns include printed materials, the Lot 1 Agency may develop production-ready artwork and recommend appropriate layouts, formats, paper stocks, finishes and printing techniques. The Agency shall provide approved print-ready artwork and specifications to whg and, where required by whg, support the supplier appointed under Lot 2 to ensure the final printed materials reflect the approved creative concept and brand standards. Lot 2 - Design, Artwork and Promotional Print Services whg requires the appointment of a single supplier to provide design, artwork and promotional print services to support the in-house Communications team. The supplier will deliver high-quality creative assets and digital and printed collateral that support corporate, internal and external communications and whg's organisational priorities. The supplier will be responsible for translating communications objectives and creative briefs into effective visual communications across digital and print channels. Services may include, but are not limited to: • Graphic design, including infographics. • Creative artwork and brand application. • Document, publication and presentation design. • Digital asset creation and social media graphics. • Promotional print production, including merchandise. • Print management and fulfilment. • Event and exhibition printed materials. The appointed supplier shall produce printed materials in accordance with approved artwork and production specifications provided or approved by whg and, where required by whg, shall work collaboratively with the Agency appointed under Lot 1 to ensure high-quality outputs. Interface between the Lots The suppliers appointed to each Lot shall demonstrate the flexibility, capacity and capability to deliver whg's requirements through a seamless and coordinated service offering. Where a requirement involves both Lots, whg may require the suppliers to work collaboratively with each other and with the in-house Communications team. Each supplier shall remain responsible for the quality, performance and delivery of the Services commissioned from it.

title: UK_1498- Arts Content Agency
description: The British Council Arts Marketing team is responsible for communicating and telling the story of the British Council’s Arts offers and programmes through digital marketing campaigns and editorial content designed for B2B and B2G audiences, with the aim of improving awareness of, engagement with and advocacy for the British Council’s Arts offers amongst key audiences and stakeholders. The appointed agency will be required to deliver video content production across a range of projects and at various scales to support the output of the British Council Arts Marketing team, with an annual budget of approximately 100k over a period of four years. This is a single supplier contract. Examples of our recent video work can be found on the British Council Arts website and YouTube channel, as well as our social media channels across Instagram, Facebook and X.

title: RA360283 - Campaign Media Buying (HIV)
description: Wales HIV Testing Week 2026 and PReP Campaign Media Buying Public Health Wales works to protect and improve the sexual health and wellbeing of people in Wales, and to reduce health inequalities. The public health objective is to continue to increase the number of people testing for HIV through a free kit online or through community venues. The communications objectives for Wales HIV Testing Week are to build knowledge about HIV and how to test, increase motivation and encourage relevant audiences to take action and test. The campaign will also build knowledge, public awareness and understanding of PReP and how to access free treatment if you are at-risk of HIV infection. Please see the attached specification for more details and instructions for bidding. All bidders must read the specification in full and upload a proposal as outlined in section 10. Failure to respond in the manner outlined will result in elimination. - To access this competition: login to https://suppliers.multiquote.com and view the opportunity RA360283. Not registered on MultiQuote - visit https://suppliers.multiquote.com then register and quote RA360283 as the reason for registration. Any queries please contact MultiQuote on 0151 482 9230.

title: 105017 - What works in AI Adoption within DCMS Sectors
buyer: Department for Culture, Media and Sport
description: DCMS are seeking to commission "what works" research into the impact and effectiveness of AI adoption interventions within DCMS sectors. We are interested in two broad sets of questions. The first is analysis of how businesses within DCMS sectors that are in the process of adopting AI achieve this, the challenges they face and the opportunities and benefits realised. We anticipate this will be explored through an ethnographic study that observes how individuals and teams actually use AI tools in their jobs. The second set of questions is what policy interventions work best to support businesses that wish to adopt AI, which we anticipate will be answered by testing hypothetical interventions through randomised control trials (RCTs). Bidders will be able to propose alternative methodologies if they think they suit these questions better; the core need for this project is to produce direct, robust evidence of what works, as opposed to what is self-reported (e.g. through interviews, focus groups, surveys, and similar) to work. This project will be commissioned either through a Competitive Flexible Procedure under the Procurement Act 2023, or through the RM6126 Research and Insights framework. This is part of the DCMS Science and Analysis R&D Programme, which supports R&D capability within the department. This project will run concurrently aside three other large projects across 2027-2030, these include; mapping the specific "user pathways" audiences take to find, consume, and value information; a continuation of previous research to develop data-intensive approaches for capturing engagement at unticketed cultural, heritage, and sporting events/activities/locations, e.g. using mobile app data to model how people participate in our events; and a continuation of previous research to design and improve methods for holistically tracking the long-term impact of major events, tested on a major event.

title: Resourcing the AI Adoption Programme
description: The GLA Group is exploring the market for an external partner to support the development and delivery of its AI Adoption Programme. The requirement is expected to include developing and embedding common AI principles across the GLA Group, supporting organisational policy and governance, designing and delivering tiered AI training, and supporting the co-design of an operating model and evaluation framework for identifying, piloting and scaling AI opportunities. This preliminary market engagement is intended to help the GLA Group understand market capability, potential delivery approaches, resourcing, indicative costs, timescales and appropriate commercial models ahead of any subsequent procurement. Participation in this exercise does not constitute a call for competition and will not influence any future procurement evaluation.

title: Behaviour Change Agency
description: Clarion's marketing strategy focuses on behaviour-change campaigns to support our residents and staff. We expect the supplier to be an expert in behaviour change and to assist Clarion Group with the marketing strategy in this area.

title: Media Buying Services, Integrated Marketing Campaigns and PR Services
description: The Welsh Government Commercial Delivery Team wish to establish a new Framework Agreement for the provision of Media Buying Services, Integrated Marketing Campaigns and PR Services. The Framework Agreement will be open for use by the Welsh Public Sector. The anticipated total Framework value is 82000000 GBP to 49500000GBP. Welsh Government will be holding an engagement event on 8th September 2026. Following the decision to abandon the previous procurement exercise, we are committed to taking time to understand supplier perspectives, lessons learned and opportunities for improvement before progressing a new procurement. Feedback gathered through this engagement will inform decisions on the scope, structure, procurement model and operation of the replacement framework. The precise scope of the Framework Agreement will be provided in the Contract Notice and Tender Documents. Please register to attend the event by midday on 1st September August 2026 via the following link https://wales.business-events.org.uk/en/events/supplier-engagement-for-the-wgcd-media-buying-integrated-marketing-campaigns-and-pr-services-framework-agreement/ where the event details will be provided and where registration will be managed. Those who register will receive confirmation of their registration. Please see the engagement section of this notice for full details.

title: Media Buying and Planning
description: Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) is seeking to engage with experienced media planning and buying agencies to inform the development of its procurement strategy and service specification. TfGM anticipates requiring a provider capable of delivering integrated media strategy, planning and buying services, with extensive experience of using strategic insight, audience intelligence and data-driven approaches to develop and deliver effective media campaigns. The successful agency would be expected to support a broad range of transport, behavioural change and customer engagement objectives across Greater Manchester. This market engagement notice will enable TfGM to develop our requirements and inform the tender specification. A Request for Information (RFI) questionnaire is available for suppliers to complete via the Pro Contract portal. Information on how to access the Pro Contract portal and this opportunity can be found further down this notice.

title: Creative and Content Framework (LSHW.005.2026)
description: Life Sciences Hub Wales seeks to procure and implement a Framework Agreement for the provision of Creative and Content Services. In this context, Creative and Content Services are defined as the strategic development, creation, and delivery of high-quality, audience-focused content and creative outputs across multiple channels, formats, and platforms. The services provided via the Creative and Content Services framework will support Life Sciences Hub Wales’s communications, engagement, marketing and brand objectives. Life Sciences Hub Wales requires the strategic development of creative content. Emphasis is placed on strategic; all creative content to be sourced via the framework is to be conceptualised and designed with intention, so that all assets align to, and where appropriate seek to improve or add value to, overarching brand identity, communication plans and campaign effectiveness. There is an overarching strategic wrap-around requirement consistent throughout all framework activity to ensure alignment, consistency and connectivity to wider brand development, content planning and campaign delivery. As such, Life Sciences Hub Wales seeks to appoint suppliers to the Creative and Content Services that have the experience, expertise and vision to design promotional materials, corporate publications, event collateral and multimedia assets with clear conceptual and strategic-alignment, as opposed to standalone designs with no consideration for wider context. The full specification is provided within the Invitation to Tender document further contextualises and defines the Life Sciences Hub Wales requirements and service expectations via the framework. Life Sciences Hub Wales envisages the ad-hoc provision of a range of design material, content and collateral. The nature of the projects and tasks required during the period of the agreement will be varied and dependent on priorities identified by Life Sciences Hub Wales. Each instance of activity as required by Life Sciences Hub Wales will be called-off via the framework as a distinct package of work, in-line with the framework governance process. The intention is to award a position on the framework to up to two (2) suppliers.

title: ITT - Digital and AI Skills Training - UID 321
description: Historic England is seeking an experienced external provider to design, deliver and continuously improve an organisation-wide Digital and AI Capability Programme as part of its AI Adoption workstream. The programme aims to accelerate the responsible adoption of digital and AI technologies by increasing confidence and practical application across the workforce. The successful supplier will help assess current levels of digital and AI maturity, identify skill gaps, provide targeted learning opportunities and support sustainable behavior change. Working closely with the AI Adoption Manager, Learning & Development team and key stakeholders, the supplier will deliver a scalable programme that supports organisational priorities and evolves in response to learner needs and developments in AI technology. Full details can be found in the invitation to tender

title: Media Buying Services for Guildhall School
buyer: The Mayor and Commonalty and Citizens of the City of London
description: The City invites Bidders to complete and submit a request to participate in the Procurement for the provision of Media Buying Services for the Guildhall School. Guildhall School is where passion meets purpose. We deliver world-class professional training in music, drama, production and design across our iconic, state-of-the-art facilities in the heart of the City of London. The School is seeking an experienced supplier to provide strategic digital media planning and buying services to support the recruitment of students, programme participants and audiences across the full range of the School’s activities. The successful supplier will be responsible for developing and delivering effective paid media strategies, ensuring that the School’s media budget is used in the most creative, efficient and impactful way possible. This will include strategic planning, media buying, campaign optimisation, performance monitoring and reporting. Suppliers with a strong track record in digital media planning and buying, particularly within the higher education sector, are invited to participate in the Invitation to Participate (ITP) stage of this procurement process. This tendering exercise is being undertaken using the electronic tendering system ‘City of London Corporation Sourcing & Contracts Portal’ (https://cityoflondon.ukp.app.jaggaer.com/) Suppliers will need to register an interest on the system in order to participate and registration is free. The estimated contract value given at sections 31 and 32 is for the full duration of the contract including the maximum possible extensions. The estimated annual contract value is therefore £225,000 exc. VAT)
